{{Short description|Topic in mathematics}}

In [[mathematics]], especially in the fields of [[group cohomology]], [[homological algebra]] and [[number theory]], the '''Lyndon spectral sequence''' or '''Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence''' is a [[spectral sequence]] relating the [[group cohomology]] of a normal subgroup ''N'' and the quotient group ''G''/''N'' to the [[cohomology]] of the total group ''G''.  The spectral sequence is named after [[Roger Lyndon]], [[Gerhard Hochschild]], and [[Jean-Pierre Serre]].  

==Statement==
Let <math>G</math> be a [[group (mathematics)|group]] and <math>N</math> be a [[normal subgroup]]. The latter ensures that the [[quotient group|quotient]] <math>G/N</math> is a group, as well. Finally, let <math>A</math> be a [[G-module|<math>G</math>-module]]. Then there is a [[spectral sequence]] of cohomological type

:<math>H^p(G/N,H^q(N,A)) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(G,A)</math>

and there is a [[spectral sequence#homological spectral sequence|spectral sequence of homological type]]

:<math>H_p(G/N,H_q(N,A)) \Longrightarrow H_{p+q}(G,A)</math>,
where the arrow '<math>\Longrightarrow</math>' means [[spectral sequence#Terms of convergence|convergence of spectral sequences]].

The same statement holds if <math>G</math> is a [[profinite group]], <math>N</math> is a ''closed'' normal subgroup and <math>H^*</math> denotes the continuous cohomology.

== Examples ==
=== Homology of the Heisenberg group ===

The spectral sequence can be used to compute the homology of the [[Heisenberg group]] ''G'' with integral entries, i.e., matrices of the form

:<math>\left ( \begin{array}{ccc} 1 & a & c \\ 0 & 1 & b \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{array} \right ), \ a, b, c \in \Z.</math>

This group is a [[Group extension#Central extension|central extension]]

:<math>0 \to \Z \to G \to \Z \oplus \Z \to 0</math>

with [[Center (group theory)|center]] <math>\Z</math> corresponding to the subgroup with <math>a=b=0</math>. The spectral sequence for the group homology, together with the analysis of a differential in this spectral sequence, shows that<ref>{{cite book|first=Kevin|last= Knudson| title=Homology of Linear Groups|series=Progress in Mathematics|volume= 193| publisher= [[Birkhäuser|Birkhäuser Verlag]]|location=Basel|year=2001| isbn = 3-7643-6415-7|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8338-2|mr=1807154}}  Example A.2.4</ref>

:<math>H_i (G, \Z) = \left \{ \begin{array}{cc} \Z & i=0, 3 \\ \Z \oplus \Z & i=1,2 \\ 0 & i>3. \end{array} \right. </math>

=== Cohomology of wreath products ===

For a group ''G'', the [[wreath product]] is an extension

:<math>1 \to G^p \to G \wr \Z / p \to \Z / p \to 1.</math>

The resulting spectral sequence of group cohomology with coefficients in a field ''k'',

:<math>H^r(\Z/p, H^s(G^p, k)) \Rightarrow H^{r+s}(G \wr \Z/p, k),</math>

is known to degenerate at the <math>E_2</math>-page.<ref>{{citation|title=Decomposition Theorem for Homology Groups of Symmetric Groups|
first=Minoru|last= Nakaoka|journal=[[Annals of Mathematics]] |series=Second Series|volume=71|issue=1|year=1960|pages=16–42|jstor=1969878|doi=10.2307/1969878}}, for a brief summary see section 2 of {{citation|last1=Carlson|first1= Jon F.|last2=Henn|first2= Hans-Werner| title=Depth and the cohomology of wreath products|journal=[[Manuscripta Mathematica]] |volume=87|issue=2|year=1995|pages=145–151|doi= 10.1007/BF02570466|citeseerx= 10.1.1.540.1310|s2cid= 27212941}}</ref>

==Properties==
The associated [[five-term exact sequence]] to the group cohomology is the usual [[inflation-restriction exact sequence]]:

:<math>0 \to H^1(G/N,A^N) \xrightarrow{\text{inf}} H^1(G,A) \xrightarrow{\text{res}}
H^1(N,A)^{G/N} \xrightarrow{d} H^2(G/N,A^N) \xrightarrow{\text{inf}} H^2(G,A).</math>

The associated [[five-term exact sequence]] to the group homology is the coinflation-corestriction exact sequence:<ref>{{cite book
 | last = Weibel
 | first = Charles A. |author-link=Charles Weibel
 | title = An Introduction to Homological Algebra
 | publisher = Cambridge University Press
 | series = Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics
 | volume = 38
 | year = 1994
 | isbn = 978-0-521-55987-4}}§ 6.8.3</ref>

:<math>H_2(G, A) \xrightarrow{\text{coinf}} H_2(G/N, A_N) \xrightarrow{d}
H_1(N, A)_{G/N} \xrightarrow{\text{cor}} H_1(G, A) \xrightarrow{\text{coinf}} H_1(G/N, A_N) \to 0. </math>

==Generalizations==
The spectral sequence is an instance of the more general [[Grothendieck spectral sequence]] of the composition of two derived functors. Indeed, <math>H^{*}(G,-)</math> is the [[derived functor]] of <math>(-)^G</math> (i.e., taking ''G''-invariants) and the composition of the functors <math>(-)^N</math> and <math>(-)^{G/N}</math> is exactly <math>(-)^G</math>.

A similar spectral sequence exists for group homology, as opposed to group cohomology.<ref>{{Citation | last1=McCleary | first1=John | title=A User's Guide to Spectral Sequences | publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] | edition=2nd | series=Cambridge Studies in Advanced Mathematics | isbn=978-0-521-56759-6 |mr=1793722 | year=2001 | volume=58}}, Theorem 8<sup>bis</sup>.12</ref>

A similar spectral sequence exists for Lie algebras. <ref>{{Citation | last1=Fuks | first1=D. B. | title=Infinite-Dimensional Lie Algebras | series=Contemporary Soviet Mathematics | isbn=978-1-4684-8767-1 | year=1986}}, Chapter 2 section 5.1 </ref>
